editions.name: Trouble Brewing
editions.description: An introductory script full of information and fairly simple abilities. The best place for a new table to start.
editions.detailNotes:
A single Imp hunts the town while information roles like the Empath, Fortune Teller, and Washerwoman teach new players how claims and cross-referencing actually work. The Poisoner is the only real deception in play, which keeps a first game honest without making it easy.

At the table, this usually plays out as a straightforward race: good tries to correlate two or three solid claims before the Imp finds a second kill, while the only real static in the signal is a single poisoned night. It's the script every other one on this list assumes you already know how to play.

editions.name: Bad Moon Rising
editions.description: A harsher, more chaotic script — outsiders lie about who they are, and the demon comes in unpredictable, asymmetric shapes.
editions.detailNotes:
Four very different demons — Zombuul, Pukka, Shabaloth, and Po — each kill on their own strange schedule, so 'who's the demon' rarely has one clean answer. The Godfather and Devil's Advocate protect evil's secrets while a Mastermind waits behind the scenes, ready to drag the game past its expected ending.

Because no single kill pattern points reliably at the demon, good has to build its case from Outsider behavior as much as night deaths — a quiet Goon or a cagey Lunatic can look exactly like a nervous evil player. A Mastermind win means the day the town finally executes the demon isn't necessarily the day the game actually ends.

editions.name: Sects & Violets
editions.description: A script of madness and misinformation, where players can't always trust their own alignment, let alone anyone else's.
editions.detailNotes:
A Cerenovus can quietly convince a townsfolk they're someone else entirely, an Evil Twin ties two fates together from the first night, and a Vortox demon can turn every true piece of information in play into a lie. By the time a Pit-Hag or Witch has finished rearranging the grimoire, no claim is safe to trust at face value.

The danger compounds rather than stays contained: once one player's claim is in doubt — mad, twinned, or just unlucky — the whole information network they were part of goes with them. And because Vortox can win without ever attacking, a good team playing a technically flawless information game can still lose the moment it forgets that.

editions.name: Everyone Can Play
editions.description: Designed for a mixed table of veterans and first-timers — almost entirely Trouble Brewing, with a Scarlet Woman's extra night-death and a Mayor/Saint's execution stakes layered on top.
editions.detailNotes:
Newer players get the same gentle information game — Empath, Fortune Teller, Librarian — while a Scarlet Woman ready to inherit the Imp and a Mayor's win-without-execution keep the more experienced half of the table just as engaged.

It changes almost nothing structurally from Trouble Brewing, which is the point — a first-timer can learn the same core loop of claims and cross-referencing, while the added stakes give returning players an actual reason to think twice before executing on a hunch.

editions.name: Hide & Seek
editions.description: Everyone is lying, or should be — a bluff-heavy script that rewards double-claims from both teams, good included.
editions.detailNotes:
Four demons — Imp, Pukka, Vigormortis, Ojo — can all plausibly be hiding behind the same early claim, and a Witch's curse waits to punish whoever nominates carelessly. The Noble, Preacher, and Pixie still hand good just enough real information to make every bluff a genuine risk.

The usual shortcut — 'good tells the truth, evil lies' — doesn't hold here, since good is bluffing too, which means an execution decision that looks safe on paper rarely feels safe in the room. A wrongly-punished claim from the Witch or Cerenovus can cost the town a truthful player just as easily as a lying one.

editions.name: Lunar Eclipse
editions.description: Can the Lunatic go an entire game without ever realizing what they are?
editions.detailNotes:
Three demons who each kill differently — Zombuul's silence, Vigormortis's poisoned inheritance, No Dashii's spreading falsehood — share the night with a Marionette who quietly believes they're on the wrong team. The Lunatic is the heart of it, but far from the only one confused about themselves.

Because the table can often piece together what the Lunatic actually is well before the Lunatic themselves does, this script carries a spectator tension the others don't — everyone watching a player confidently act on a belief that isn't true. Three demons with three different kill rhythms keep the rest of the town honestly unsure what's actually happening at night, Lunatic aside.

editions.name: Trust
editions.description: Built around keeping the Mayor's alternate win condition alive and contested — safety nets and threats to it on both sides.
editions.detailNotes:
A Politician can flip a losing game to good from beyond the grave, while a Marionette and a Witch make sure evil always has a way to unsettle the town's trust in exactly who deserves protecting. Every execution here carries the weight of the Mayor's win looming behind it.

Good has to weigh protecting the Mayor's win against actively hunting evil, since a quiet day that keeps the Mayor alive can also be exactly what a Marionette or Witch needs to keep operating unnoticed. Evil, in turn, has to decide whether disrupting that quiet is worth the exposure it risks.

editions.name: Boozling
editions.description: A high-tension chaos script built around Fang Gu and Baron threats, with Cerenovus madness thrown into the mix.
editions.detailNotes:
A Golem can end the game with a single wrong nomination, a Cannibal inherits whatever the town just executed, and a High Priestess or Fisherman hand out just enough truth to make the chaos feel survivable. Fang Gu's jump and Baron's extra outsiders mean the setup itself is never quite what it first looks like.

Few games here play out the same way twice — a Golem's nomination can end things in a single day one game and never come up the next, and a Cannibal picking up whatever ability the town just executed means the town's own choices keep reshaping what they're up against.

editions.name: The Minotaur's Labyrinth
editions.description: An information-forward script — plenty to learn, and a Cannibal ready to inherit whatever the town executes.
editions.detailNotes:
Three roaming demons — Shabaloth, Po, Fang Gu — alongside the Imp keep the killer's identity shifting even as the Investigator, Fortune Teller, and Clockmaker pile up clues about it. A Politician and Recluse make sure good's information is never quite as safe as it looks.

Solid information goes stale fast when the demon threatening the town could be any of three very different shapes on a given night, so a Fortune Teller or Clockmaker's read from two nights ago may already be worthless. A Politician or Recluse muddies even who's safe to trust with that information in the first place.

editions.name: The Wrong Name
editions.description: A demon that kills by character, not by face — and a town that has to work out which roles even still exist to protect them.
editions.detailNotes:
Ojo doesn't choose a player — it chooses a character, and if that character isn't in the game, the Storyteller decides who actually dies. An Evil Twin ties two fates together from night one, and a Pit-Hag can turn a townsfolk into something else entirely, so the character list Ojo is aiming at keeps quietly changing underneath it.

Good's usual shortcuts don't fully apply here: naming a character as safe doesn't mean naming a player as safe, and a Golem's single nomination or a drunk Puzzlemaster can end a game in one move if the town aims it wrong. Fang Gu's jump onto an Outsider only adds to how little the board resembles what it looked like at the start of the night.

editions.name: Overtime
editions.description: Built to outlast the moment good thinks it's won — a Mastermind who plays on past the Demon's execution, and Outsiders whose real cost lands only after they're already gone.
editions.detailNotes:
Mastermind's whole point is a day that keeps going after the town is sure it's over — a Snake Charmer or Lycanthrope give good real teeth to end things decisively, but a Scarlet Woman is still ready to inherit if they don't move fast enough. A Sweetheart or Moonchild's own death doesn't end their impact either; it just changes shape.

The table has to plan past the execution it's aiming for, not just toward it — a nomination that looks like a clean win can still leave a Mastermind's one extra day to punish a careless guess. Goon and Tinker round out an unusually large Outsider bench, which a Godfather is only too happy to pick off.

editions.name: Last Rites
editions.description: Every script has stakes, but here a single nomination can end the game outright — a Saint, a Golem, or a Damsel each turn one specific moment into the whole ballgame.
editions.detailNotes:
A Saint executed is an instant evil win, a Golem's one lifetime nomination kills outright if they're wrong, and a Damsel correctly guessed by a Minion ends it just as fast — three completely different players who can each single-handedly decide the game before the Demon ever gets a say. A Devil's Advocate is there specifically to protect the wrong one of them at the worst possible time.

Po and Shabaloth keep the night threat itself unpredictable — one holds its kill and unloads three at once, the other might bring its last victim back with it — so the town rarely gets a clean read on when the real danger is even coming. Every nomination has to be weighed against what it could cost beyond just who dies.

editions.name: First Blood
editions.description: A tight five-to-seven player table's first taste of the game — classic roles, one Demon, nothing to overthink.
editions.detailNotes:
Built small on purpose — Washerwoman, Empath, and Chef teach the basic claim-and-cross-reference loop, a Slayer and Virgin give good a couple of real swings, and a single Imp keeps the night threat simple to track at a table this size.

With so few seats, every piece of information carries more weight than it would at a full table — a wrong claim or a rushed execution costs the town a much bigger share of what little it has to work with.

editions.name: Small Mercies
editions.description: A gentler five-to-seven player table, thick with protective Outsiders and a Demon who doesn't always strike when you expect.
editions.detailNotes:
A Saint's life is worth protecting and a Drunk quietly wastes an ability without anyone knowing which one, while Fortune Teller, Investigator, and Librarian hand out real information early. Pukka's poison doesn't always show itself the night it's given, so a death can land a full day later than the town expects.

A Spy or Assassin only needs one good read to turn a quiet game sharply — Grandmother's known Townsfolk becomes a real anchor to build the rest of the table's trust around, right up until Assassin removes them outright.

editions.name: No Greater Joy
editions.description: A simple 'next step' for new players who have played Trouble Brewing — official Teensyville by Steven Medway.
editions.detailNotes:
Steven Medway's own recommended first Teensyville table: a Clockmaker, Investigator, and Empath keep the information game familiar to anyone who's played Trouble Brewing, while a Sage gives good one real answer even if the Demon gets them. A Scarlet Woman and Baron are the only real complication — small enough that a wrong guess doesn't spiral.

With just two Outsiders on the sheet, a Baron who'd normally claim two ends up taking whatever's actually left — the same real constraint the official script itself calls out, not a house rule invented here. At a table this size, that one Klutz or Drunk carries a lot more weight per player than it would in a full game.

editions.name: Over the River
editions.description: "What big eyes you have!" — official Teensyville by Andrew Nathenson.
editions.detailNotes:
A Grandmother's known Townsfolk and a Snake Charmer willing to hunt directly give good real footing, while a Godfather decides on a whim whether the Outsider count grows or shrinks. A Recluse is there specifically to look like something it isn't — the whole table is one long game of not trusting the first thing you see.

A Lunatic adds a second layer of the same misdirection from the good side, quietly acting on a false belief about themselves while everyone else tries to read the real threat. Innkeeper and Professor round out a small table that still has real texture to it, not just a shrunk-down Trouble Brewing.

characters.name: Minion Info
characters.ability: If there are 7 or more players in play, the Minions learn which player is the Demon. If more than one Minion is in play, they also learn who the other Minions are.
characters.firstNightReminder: If there are 7 or more players in play: if more than one Minion is in play, wake all Minions together and let them make eye contact with each other. Show the 'This is the Demon' info token, then point to the Demon player. (Skip this step entirely with 6 or fewer players.)

characters.name: Demon Info
characters.ability: If there are 7 or more players in play, the Demon learns which players are the Minions, and is shown 3 good characters not in play to use as bluffs.
characters.firstNightReminder: If there are 7 or more players in play: wake the Demon. Show the 'These are your Minions' info token and point to each Minion in turn. Then show the 'These characters are not in play' info token and display 3 character tokens of good characters not in play, for the Demon to use as bluffs. (Skip this step entirely with 6 or fewer players.)

characters.name: Washerwoman
characters.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Townsfolk.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the character token of a Townsfolk in play. Point to two players, one of which is that character.

characters.name: Librarian
characters.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Outsider. (Or that zero are in play.)
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the character token of an Outsider in play. Point to two players, one of which is that character.

characters.name: Investigator
characters.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Minion.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the character token of a Minion in play. Point to two players, one of which is that character.

characters.name: Chef
characters.ability: You start knowing how many pairs of evil players there are.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the finger signal (0, 1, 2, ...) for the number of pairs of neighbouring evil players.

characters.name: Empath
characters.ability: Each night, you learn how many of your 2 alive neighbours are evil.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the finger signal (0, 1, 2) for the number of evil alive neighbours of the Empath.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the finger signal (0, 1, 2) for the number of evil alive neighbours of the Empath.

characters.name: Fortune Teller
characters.ability: Each night, choose 2 players: you learn if either is a Demon. There is a good player that registers as a Demon to you.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Fortune Teller points to two players. Give the head signal (nod 'yes', shake 'no') for whether one of those players is the Demon.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Fortune Teller points to two players. Show the head signal (nod 'yes', shake 'no') for whether one of those players is the Demon.

characters.name: Undertaker
characters.ability: Each night*, you learn which character died by execution today.
characters.otherNightReminder: If a player was executed today: show that player's character token.

characters.name: Monk
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player (not yourself): they are safe from the Demon tonight.
characters.otherNightReminder: The previously protected player is no longer protected. The Monk points to a player, not themself. Mark that player 'Protected'.

characters.name: Ravenkeeper
characters.ability: If you die at night, you are woken to choose a player: you learn their character.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Ravenkeeper died tonight: the Ravenkeeper points to a player. Show that player's character token.

characters.name: Virgin
characters.ability: The 1st time you are nominated, if the nominator is a Townsfolk, they are executed immediately.

characters.name: Slayer
characters.ability: Once per game, during the day, publicly choose a player: if they are the Demon, they die.

characters.name: Soldier
characters.ability: You are safe from the Demon.

characters.name: Mayor
characters.ability: If only 3 players live & no execution occurs, your team wins. If you die at night, another player might die instead.

characters.name: Butler
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): tomorrow, you may only vote if they are voting too.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Butler points to a player. Mark that player as 'Master'.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Butler points to a player. Mark that player as 'Master'.

characters.name: Drunk
characters.ability: You do not know you are the Drunk. You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not.

characters.name: Recluse
characters.ability: You might register as evil & as a Minion or Demon, even if dead.

characters.name: Saint
characters.ability: If you die by execution, your team loses.

characters.name: Poisoner
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned tonight and tomorrow day.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Poisoner points to a player. That player is poisoned.
characters.otherNightReminder: The previously poisoned player is no longer poisoned. The Poisoner points to a player. That player is poisoned.

characters.name: Spy
characters.ability: Each night, you see the Grimoire. You might register as good & as a Townsfolk or Outsider, even if dead.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Grimoire to the Spy for as long as they need.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the Grimoire to the Spy for as long as they need.

characters.name: Scarlet Woman
characters.ability: If there are 5 or more players alive & the Demon dies, you become the Demon. (Travellers don't count.)
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Scarlet Woman became the Demon today: show the 'You are' card, then the Demon token.

characters.name: Baron
characters.ability: There are extra Outsiders in play. [+2 Outsiders]

characters.name: Imp
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. If you kill yourself this way, a Minion becomes the Imp.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Imp points to a player. That player dies. If the Imp chose themselves: replace the character of 1 alive Minion with a spare Imp token. Show that player the 'You are' card, then the Imp token.

characters.name: Grandmother
characters.ability: You start knowing a good player & their character. If the Demon kills them, you die too.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the marked character token. Point to the marked player.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Grandmother's grandchild was killed by the Demon tonight: the Grandmother dies.

characters.name: Sailor
characters.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: either you or they are drunk until dusk. You can't die.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Sailor points to a living player. Either the Sailor, or the chosen player, is drunk.
characters.otherNightReminder: The previously drunk player is no longer drunk. The Sailor points to a living player. Either the Sailor, or the chosen player, is drunk.

characters.name: Chambermaid
characters.ability: Each night, choose 2 alive players (not yourself): you learn how many woke tonight due to their ability.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Chambermaid points to two players. Show the number signal (0, 1, 2, ...) for how many of those players wake tonight for their ability.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Chambermaid points to two players. Show the number signal (0, 1, 2, ...) for how many of those players wake tonight for their ability.

characters.name: Exorcist
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player (different to last night): the Demon, if chosen, learns who you are then doesn't wake tonight.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Exorcist points to a player, different from the previous night. If that player is the Demon: wake the Demon, show the Exorcist token, and point to the Exorcist. The Demon does not act tonight.

characters.name: Innkeeper
characters.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they can't die tonight, but 1 is drunk until dusk.
characters.otherNightReminder: The previously protected and drunk players lose those markers. The Innkeeper points to two players. Those players are protected. One of them is drunk.

characters.name: Gambler
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player & guess their character: if you guess wrong, you die.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Gambler points to a player, and names a character. If the guess is incorrect, the Gambler dies.

characters.name: Gossip
characters.ability: Each day, you may make a public statement. Tonight, if it was true, a player dies.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Gossip's public statement was true: choose a player not otherwise protected from dying tonight. That player dies.

characters.name: Courtier
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a character: they are drunk for 3 nights & 3 days.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Courtier either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a character on their character sheet. If they chose a character and it is in play, that player is drunk (mark 'Drunk 3').
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Courtier has an active 'Drunk' marker, reduce its remaining count by one (Drunk 3 -> Drunk 2 -> Drunk 1 -> remove). If the Courtier has not yet used their ability: the Courtier either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a character on their character sheet. If they chose a character and it is in play, that player is drunk.

characters.name: Professor
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a dead player: if they are a Townsfolk, they are resurrected.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Professor has not used their ability: the Professor either shakes their head 'no', or points to a player. If that player is a dead Townsfolk, they are now alive.

characters.name: Minstrel
characters.ability: When a Minion dies by execution, all other players (except Travellers) are drunk until dusk tomorrow.

characters.name: Tea Lady
characters.ability: If both your alive neighbours are good, they can't die.

characters.name: Pacifist
characters.ability: Executed good players might not die.

characters.name: Fool
characters.ability: The first time you die, you don't.

characters.name: Tinker
characters.ability: You might die at any time.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Tinker might die (Storyteller's discretion).

characters.name: Moonchild
characters.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player. Tonight, if it was a good player, they die.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Moonchild used their ability to target a player today: if that player is good, they die.

characters.name: Goon
characters.ability: Each night, the 1st player to choose you with their ability is drunk until dusk. You become their alignment.

characters.name: Lunatic
characters.ability: You think you are a Demon, but you are not. The Demon knows who you are & who you choose at night.
characters.firstNightReminder: If there are 7 or more players: show the Lunatic a number of arbitrary 'Minion' player positions equal to the number of Minions in play, and show 3 character tokens of arbitrary good characters as fake bluffs. If the token the Lunatic receives as their 'demon' identity is one that would wake tonight, allow the Lunatic to perform the demon-style actions and place their 'attack' markers accordingly. Afterwards, wake the real Demon, show them the Lunatic player, and if the Lunatic marked any players, show the real Demon which players were marked.
characters.otherNightReminder: Allow the Lunatic to perform the Demon's actions and place their 'attack' markers. If the Lunatic selected players: wake the Demon, show the 'attack' marker(s), then point to each marked player. Remove the Lunatic's 'attack' markers.

characters.name: Godfather
characters.ability: You start knowing which Outsiders are in play. If 1 died today, choose a player tonight: they die. [-1 or +1 Outsider]
characters.firstNightReminder: Show each of the Outsider tokens in play.
characters.otherNightReminder: If an Outsider died today: the Godfather points to a player. That player dies.

characters.name: Devil's Advocate
characters.ability: Each night, choose a living player (different to last night): if executed tomorrow, they don't die.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Devil's Advocate points to a living player. That player survives execution tomorrow.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Devil's Advocate points to a living player, different from the previous night. That player survives execution tomorrow.

characters.name: Assassin
characters.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: they die, even if for some reason they could not.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Assassin has not yet used their ability: the Assassin either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a player. That player dies.

characters.name: Mastermind
characters.ability: If the Demon dies by execution (ending the game), play for 1 more day. If a player is then executed, their team loses.

characters.name: Zombuul
characters.ability: Each night*, if no-one died today, choose a player: they die. The 1st time you die, you live but register as dead.
characters.otherNightReminder: If no-one died during the day: the Zombuul points to a player. That player dies.

characters.name: Pukka
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned. The previously poisoned player dies then becomes healthy.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Pukka points to a player. That player is poisoned.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Pukka points to a player. That player is poisoned. The previously poisoned player dies, then becomes healthy.

characters.name: Shabaloth
characters.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they die. A dead player you chose last night might be regurgitated.
characters.otherNightReminder: A player that the Shabaloth chose the previous night might be resurrected (Storyteller's choice). The Shabaloth points to two players. Those players die.

characters.name: Po
characters.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player: they die. If your last choice was no-one, choose 3 players tonight.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Po chose no-one the previous night: the Po points to three players, all of whom die. Otherwise: the Po either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a player, who dies.

characters.name: Clockmaker
characters.ability: You start knowing how many steps from the Demon to its nearest Minion.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the hand signal for the number (1, 2, 3, etc.) of places from the Demon to the closest Minion.

characters.name: Dreamer
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself or Travellers): you learn 1 good and 1 evil character, 1 of which is correct.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Dreamer points to a player. Show 1 good and 1 evil character token; one of these is that player's correct character.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Dreamer points to a player. Show 1 good and 1 evil character token; one of these is that player's correct character.

characters.name: Snake Charmer
characters.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: a chosen Demon swaps characters & alignments with you & is then poisoned.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Snake Charmer points to a player. If that player is the Demon: swap the Demon and Snake Charmer characters and alignments. Wake each player to inform them of their new role and alignment. The new Snake Charmer is poisoned.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Snake Charmer points to a player. If that player is the Demon: swap the Demon and Snake Charmer characters and alignments. Wake each player to inform them of their new role and alignment. The new Snake Charmer is poisoned.

characters.name: Mathematician
characters.ability: Each night, you learn how many players' abilities worked abnormally (since dawn) due to another character's ability.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the hand signal for the number (0, 1, 2, etc.) of players whose ability malfunctioned due to another character's ability.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the hand signal for the number (0, 1, 2, etc.) of players whose ability malfunctioned due to another character's ability.

characters.name: Flowergirl
characters.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Demon voted today.
characters.otherNightReminder: Nod 'yes' or shake head 'no' for whether a Demon voted today. Place the 'Demon voted' or 'Demon not voted' marker as appropriate.

characters.name: Town Crier
characters.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Minion nominated today.
characters.otherNightReminder: Nod 'yes' or shake head 'no' for whether a Minion nominated today. Place the 'Minion nominated' or 'Minion not nominated' marker as appropriate.

characters.name: Oracle
characters.ability: Each night*, you learn how many dead players are evil.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the hand signal for the number (0, 1, 2, etc.) of dead players who are evil.

characters.name: Savant
characters.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller to learn 2 things in private: 1 is true & 1 is false.

characters.name: Seamstress
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, choose 2 players (not yourself): you learn if they are the same alignment.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Seamstress either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to two other players. If the Seamstress chose players, nod 'yes' or shake 'no' for whether they are the same alignment.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Seamstress has not yet used their ability: the Seamstress either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to two other players. If the Seamstress chose players, nod 'yes' or shake 'no' for whether they are the same alignment.

characters.name: Philosopher
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a good character: gain that ability. If this character is in play, they are drunk.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Philosopher either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a good character on their character sheet. If they chose a character: swap the out-of-play character token onto the Philosopher and add the 'Is the Philosopher' reminder. If the character is in play, place the 'Drunk' marker on that player.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Philosopher has not used their ability: the Philosopher either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to a good character on their character sheet. If they chose a character: swap the out-of-play character token onto the Philosopher and add the 'Is the Philosopher' reminder. If the character is in play, place the 'Drunk' marker on that player.

characters.name: Artist
characters.ability: Once per game, during the day, privately ask the Storyteller any yes/no question.

characters.name: Juggler
characters.ability: On your 1st day, publicly guess up to 5 players' characters. That night, you learn how many you got correct.
characters.otherNightReminder: If today was the Juggler's first day: show the hand signal for the number (0, 1, 2, etc.) of 'Correct' markers, then remove those markers.

characters.name: Sage
characters.ability: If the Demon kills you, you learn that it is 1 of 2 players.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Sage was killed by the Demon: point to two players, one of which is that Demon.

characters.name: Mutant
characters.ability: If you are “mad” about being an Outsider, you might be executed.

characters.name: Sweetheart
characters.ability: When you die, 1 player is drunk from now on.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Sweetheart died today: choose a player (Storyteller's choice). That player is drunk from now on.

characters.name: Barber
characters.ability: If you died today or tonight, the Demon may choose 2 players (not another Demon) to swap characters.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Barber died today: wake the Demon. Show the 'This character selected you' card, then the Barber token. The Demon either shows the 'no' head signal, or points to 2 players (not another Demon). If they chose players: swap those two players' character tokens, then wake each player and show them the 'You are' card followed by their new character token.

characters.name: Klutz
characters.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player: if they are evil, your team loses.

characters.name: Evil Twin
characters.ability: You & an opposing player know each other. If the good player is executed, evil wins. Good can't win if you both live.
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the Evil Twin and their Twin together. Point to the Evil Twin and show the Twin player the Evil Twin token. Point to the Twin and show the Evil Twin player the Twin's character token. Confirm both have acknowledged each other.

characters.name: Witch
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: if they nominate tomorrow, they die. If just 3 players live, you lose this ability.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Witch points to a player. If that player nominates tomorrow, they die immediately.
characters.otherNightReminder: If there are 4 or more players alive: the Witch points to a player. If that player nominates tomorrow, they die immediately.

characters.name: Cerenovus
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player & a good character: they are “mad” they are this character tomorrow, or might be executed.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Cerenovus points to a player, then to a good character on their character sheet. Wake that player, show them the 'This character selected you' card, then the Cerenovus token, then the selected character token. If the player is not 'mad' about being that character tomorrow, they can be executed.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Cerenovus points to a player, then to a good character on their character sheet. Wake that player, show them the 'This character selected you' card, then the Cerenovus token, then the selected character token. If the player is not 'mad' about being that character tomorrow, they can be executed.

characters.name: Pit-Hag
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player & a character they become (if not-in-play). If a Demon is made, deaths tonight are arbitrary.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Pit-Hag points to a player, then to a character on the character sheet. If that character is not in play, wake the chosen player and show them the 'You are' card, then the relevant character token. If the character is already in play, nothing happens.

characters.name: Fang Gu
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The 1st Outsider this kills becomes an evil Fang Gu & you die instead. [+1 Outsider]
characters.otherNightReminder: The Fang Gu points to a player. That player dies. However, if that player was an Outsider and there are no other Fang Gu in play: the Fang Gu dies instead of the chosen player, and the chosen player becomes an evil Fang Gu. Wake the new Fang Gu, show them the 'You are' card, then the Fang Gu token, then the 'You are' card and the thumbs-down 'evil' hand sign.

characters.name: Vigormortis
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Minions you kill keep their ability & poison 1 Townsfolk neighbour. [-1 Outsider]
characters.otherNightReminder: The Vigormortis points to a player. That player dies. If they were a Minion, they keep their ability and one of their Townsfolk neighbours becomes poisoned.

characters.name: No Dashii
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Your 2 Townsfolk neighbours are poisoned.
characters.otherNightReminder: The No Dashii points to a player. That player dies.

characters.name: Vortox
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Townsfolk abilities yield false info. Each day, if no-one is executed, evil wins.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Vortox points to a player. That player dies.

characters.name: Steward
characters.ability: You start knowing 1 good player.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Steward a good player.

characters.name: Knight
characters.ability: You start knowing 2 players that are not the Demon.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Knight 2 players, neither of which is the Demon.

characters.name: Shugenja
characters.ability: You start knowing if your closest evil player is clockwise or anti-clockwise. If equidistant, this info is arbitrary.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Shugenja the clockwise or anti-clockwise token.

characters.name: Bounty Hunter
characters.ability: You start knowing 1 evil player. If the player you know dies, you learn another evil player tonight.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Bounty Hunter an evil player. Place the Know reminder on that player.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the player with the Know reminder has died, show the Bounty Hunter a new evil player and move the reminder.

characters.name: Noble
characters.ability: You start knowing 3 players, 1 and only 1 of which is evil.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Noble 3 players, exactly 1 of which is evil.

characters.name: Balloonist
characters.ability: Each night, you learn 1 player of each character type, until there are no more types to learn.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Balloonist a player of a character type they haven't yet learned.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the Balloonist a player of a character type they haven't yet learned, if any remain.

characters.name: Golem
characters.ability: You may only nominate once per game. When you do, if the nominee is not the Demon, they die.

characters.name: Magician
characters.ability: The Demon thinks you are a Minion. Minions think you are a Demon.

characters.name: Puzzlemaster
characters.ability: 1 player is drunk, even if you die. If you guess (once) who it is, learn the Demon player, but guess wrong & get false info.
characters.firstNightReminder: If the Puzzlemaster wishes to guess, they point to a player. Confirm correct/incorrect, and if correct, show the Demon.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Puzzlemaster wishes to guess (and hasn't yet), they point to a player. Confirm correct/incorrect, and if correct, show the Demon.

characters.name: Preacher
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: a Minion, if chosen, learns this. All chosen Minions have no ability.
characters.firstNightReminder: The Preacher points to a player. If they are a Minion, nod to confirm and show them the Preacher token.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Preacher points to a player. If they are a Minion, nod to confirm and show them the Preacher token.

characters.name: Pixie
characters.ability: You start knowing 1 in-play Townsfolk. If you were mad that you were this character, you gain their ability when they die.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the Pixie a Townsfolk player in play.

characters.name: Ojo
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a character: they die. If they are not in play, the Storyteller chooses who dies.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Ojo names a character. Whoever holds it dies; if nobody does, choose who dies.

characters.name: Damsel
characters.ability: All Minions know you are in play. If a Minion publicly guesses you (once), your team loses.

characters.name: Huntsman
characters.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a living player: the Damsel, if chosen, becomes a not-in-play Townsfolk.
characters.firstNightReminder: If the Huntsman wishes to choose (once, ever), they point to a player. If that player is the Damsel, she becomes a not-in-play Townsfolk.
characters.otherNightReminder: If the Huntsman wishes to choose (once, ever, and hasn't yet), they point to a player. If that player is the Damsel, she becomes a not-in-play Townsfolk.

characters.name: Lycanthrope
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a living player: if good, they die, but they are the only player that can die tonight.
characters.otherNightReminder: The Lycanthrope points to a player. If good, that player dies, and no one else can die tonight.

characters.name: Cannibal
characters.ability: You have the ability of the recently killed executee. If they are evil, you are poisoned until a good player dies by execution.

characters.name: Marionette
characters.ability: You think you are a good character but you are not. The Demon knows who you are.

characters.name: General
characters.ability: Each night, you learn which alignment the Storyteller believes is winning: good, evil, or neither.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the General the good, evil, or neither signal for who is believed to be winning.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the General the good, evil, or neither signal for who is believed to be winning.

characters.name: Politician
characters.ability: If you were the player most responsible for your team losing, you change alignment & win, even if dead.

characters.name: High Priestess
characters.ability: Each night, learn which player the Storyteller believes you should talk to most.
characters.firstNightReminder: Show the High Priestess a player.
characters.otherNightReminder: Show the High Priestess a player.

characters.name: Fisherman
characters.ability: Once per game, during the day, visit the Storyteller for some advice to help you win.
